sources.title: Xintiandi Shanghai Travel Guide (2026): Shopping, Dining & History
sources.content:
Xintiandi is a revitalized historic district in Shanghai's Huangpu District, located at 245 Madang Road. Open 24 hours, free entry, recommended 4 hours for a visit.

The district originated in the 1920s-1930s. A revitalization project in 1998 transformed Xintiandi into a vibrant hub for dining, shopping, and entertainment while preserving its historic charm. Features distinctive Shikumen architecture—traditional stone-gate houses unique to Shanghai.

Site of the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China located at 374 Huangpi South Road, Tuesday-Sunday 9 AM-5 PM, free admission.

Shopping: Arket (Nordic minimalist fashion with café), Studious (Japanese multi-brand boutique), looknow lab (Jellycat plush toys), Harmay (discounted beauty retailer).

Dining: Cova (premium café), Verie (beautifully crafted croissants), Tea'stone (Chinese aesthetics with tea and desserts), Yuan Gu Yun Jing (creative Chinese cuisine).

Transportation: From Pudong Airport: Metro Line 2 to Century Avenue, transfer to Line 9 (~1 hour 20 minutes, 8 RMB). Within Shanghai: Metro Lines 8, 9, or 13 to Xintiandi Station (Exit 3).

sources.title: How to Visit Xintiandi - China Travel Tips
sources.content:
Xintiandi is divided into two parts: the South Block and the North Block, where the South Block mainly consists of modern architecture while the North Block keeps the old Shikumen architecture style.

Take Metro Line 10/Line 13 to Xintiandi Station and get out from Exit 6 to Madang Road, then walk a bit to the north.

Xintiandi is a modern paradise for foodies, shoppers, and culture enthusiasts, featuring an eclectic mix of high-end fashion boutiques, exquisite dining options, and vibrant entertainment venues.

Highly accessible with flat pathways, wide roads, and elevators in most malls and restaurants, very accommodating for families and visitors with mobility needs.

Fuxing Park close to Xintiandi is Shanghai's only French-style park with wide tree-lined walkways and amazing flower beds.

sources.title: 上海新天地_百度百科
sources.content:
上海新天地位于上海市黄浦区，是一处由香港瑞安集团于2001年建成的休闲步行街。以上海的石库门建筑旧区为基础改造，采用存表去里的设计手法，保留建筑外观和历史风貌。

新天地分为南北两部分：北里以保留石库门旧建筑为主，南里以现代建筑为主，包含总楼面面积达25,000平方米的购物娱乐中心。

项目总投资约1.5亿美元，1999年初动工，2001年底建成。设计师引入现代化设施（光纤电缆、空调系统等），为强调历史感保留原有砖瓦，从德国进口防潮药水注射进墙壁。

石库门住宅兴起于19世纪60年代，曾占上海市区全部住宅面积的六成以上。融合中西特色，成为近代上海历史文化的重要标志。

2025年新增东台里商业体，增加8.8万平方米开放式空间和6500平方米全景天幕。

2020年入选上海新十大地标建筑；2003年获Urban Land Institute Award for Excellence大奖。

sources.title: Xintiandi Travel Guide: Map, Shopping, Restaurants & Hotels
sources.content:
Xintiandi is a famous pedestrian street in Shanghai's Huangpu District. Divided into South Block (modern architecture) and North Block (traditional Shikumen style).

Notable dining establishments include international restaurants and traditional tea houses. Shopping features luxury brands alongside local designers.

The area is accessible via Metro Line 10 or 13 to Xintiandi Station. Open 24/7 with free admission.

sources.title: Xintiandi Shanghai - Highlights, Restaurants, Hotels, Bars, Shopping
sources.content:
Xintiandi is one of Shanghai's most popular lifestyle destinations combining historic Shikumen architecture with modern entertainment and dining. The area features boutiques, art galleries, cafés, and a vibrant nightlife scene.

The First National Congress of CPC site is located here, making it historically significant. Restaurant options range from Michelin-starred establishments to casual eateries.

Best time to visit is afternoon through evening when the atmosphere is most vibrant. The area is well-lit and safe at night.

sources.title: Xintiandi, Shanghai – Area Combining Old Shikumen & Modern Fashion
sources.content:
Xintiandi is a famous lifestyle destination combining traditional Shikumen architecture with modern dining, shopping, and entertainment. Located in Huangpu District, it features a mix of historic stone-gate houses and contemporary buildings.

The area is divided into North Block (preserved old buildings) and South Block (modern architecture). Notable attractions include the Site of the First National Congress of the CPC.

The neighborhood offers international dining, boutique shopping, art galleries, and vibrant nightlife. The area is well-lit, safe, and accessible via Metro Lines 10 and 13 to Xintiandi Station.

Best visited in the evening when restaurants and bars come alive. Free to enter and open 24/7.
